requirements.requirement: Rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: The installed logrotate policy specifies daily rotation, seven retained rotations, and compression. The system-wide daily timer is enabled and active. A forced functional rotation produced a valid gzip archive, and the policy persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing through a rotation.
requirements.summary: A file descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote afterward. The active file retained the same inode and contained the post-rotation record, while the pre-rotation data appeared in the compressed archive.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged from the prepared baseline through the final restarted state. The existing logrotate 3.21.0 installation successfully parsed and executed the policy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is complete and coherent: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by the lifecycle snapshot, and recovered system, scheduler, policy, active-log, archive, OS, and kernel state.
limitations: Only one functional rotation was observed; seven-cycle retention is established by the validated policy rather than by creating eight successive archives.
Writer continuity was tested with a representative open append descriptor because no running inventory application process or service was present in the captured baseline.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the policy was the required implementation (cmd-e54a0b1f11c0416d); the temporary source file was removed. Test writes and the forced rotation were bounded functional evidence directly tied to rotation and writer continuity (cmd-22679497666b477e). The reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-abe529f065f04b72). No failed services, damaged package state, unsafe new listeners, or abandoned temporary files were observed afterward.
